title: The war started because of greed.
paragraphs: The war started because of greed.

Kings clashed in the Valley of Siddim.
Armies marched.
Cities fell.
And in the middle of the chaos… a man who never should have been there was carried away in chains.
His name was Lot.

Lot once walked beside Abraham.
Lot once saw the blessing of God up close.
Lot once had a front-row seat to faith.
But one decision changed everything.
He chose Sodom.
Not overnight.

First, he looked toward Sodom (Genesis 13:10).
Then he pitched his tent near Sodom (Genesis 13:12).
Later, he lived inside Sodom (Genesis 14:12).
Sin rarely begins with a leap.

It begins with a glance.
A compromise.
A small step closer to what God warned you about.

And then one day, the thing you thought you could manage…
manages you.

When invading kings swept through the region, they captured the cities of the plain.
Sodom fell.
And Lot—along with women, children, servants, and possessions—was taken away.
Bound.
Powerless.
Humiliated.
Genesis 14:12 says plainly:
“They also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who was dwelling in Sodom, and his possessions, and went their way.”
Lot had chased prosperity.
Instead, he found captivity.
But this is where the story explodes with grace.
Because someone escaped the battle and ran to tell Abraham.
And when Abraham heard what happened…
He didn’t shrug.
He didn’t say, “Well, Lot chose that life.”
He didn’t say, “That’s what compromise gets you.”
He moved.
Genesis 14:14 tells us:
“When Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, 318 of them, and went in pursuit.”
Let that sink in.
Three hundred and eighteen men.
Against an army of conquering kings.
Humanly speaking, it was impossible.
But love does things that logic cannot explain.
Abram pursued them all the way to Dan, then attacked by night.
The battle erupted under the cover of darkness.
Steel clashed.
Torches burned.
Chaos exploded in the night air.
And the impossible happened.
Genesis 14:16 says:
“Then he brought back all the possessions, and also brought back his kinsman Lot with his possessions, and the women and the people.”
Lot walked out of captivity because someone came for him.
Don’t miss this.
Lot didn’t fight his way out.
Lot didn’t earn his rescue.
Lot didn’t organize the mission.
Lot was rescued.
And right there—thousands of years before the cross—we see a shadow of the Gospel.
Because Lot is not just Lot.
Lot is us.
We look toward Sodom.
We flirt with compromise.
We convince ourselves we can live close to sin without being captured by it.
We say things like:

“Just this once.”
“No one will know.”
“I can handle it.”
Until the day comes when the chains tighten.
Addiction.
Shame.
Hidden sin.
Broken relationships.
A heart that feels far from God.
And suddenly we realize something terrifying:
We cannot rescue ourselves.
But the Bible reveals a God who pursues captives.
Just as Abram rode into battle for Lot…
Jesus stepped into history for us.
But the enemy Jesus faced was far greater than ancient kings.
He confronted sin, death, and the power of hell itself.
Colossians 2:15 says:
“He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in Him.”
At the cross, Jesus entered the battlefield.
Not with a sword.
With a cross.
Not to risk His life.
To give it.
Our Deliverer didn’t merely chase the enemy away.
He crushed the power that held us captive.
Three days later, the stone rolled away.
The grave lost.
And the Rescuer walked out alive.
This means something powerful for you today.
Your captivity is not stronger than Christ.
Your past does not disqualify you.
Your worst mistake does not have the final word.
You may feel like Lot—trapped by the consequences of choices you regret.
But hear this clearly:
Jesus still rescues.
He still pursues the lost.
He still breaks chains.
He still restores what shame tried to bury.
Luke 19:10 says:
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
Seek.
That means He comes looking.
Save.
That means He brings people out alive.
So if you’re standing too close to Sodom today…
Come back.
If compromise has quietly crept into your life…
Turn around.
If shame tells you it’s too late…
Don’t believe the lie.
The Gospel is the announcement that the Rescuer has already gone to war for you.
Repent.
Call on Christ.
Walk out of captivity and into freedom.
Because the same God who sent Abraham to rescue Lot…
Sent His Son to rescue the world.
And His rescue mission is still happening right now.
Someone reading this needs to hear it.
Someone reading this needs hope.
Someone reading this needs to know:
Your story is not over.
Jesus still rescues.
Someone you know may be waiting for the very rescue this story reveals.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
